growth.label: Producer net growth
growth.effect: Sets the intrinsic rate r₁ before interactions.

interaction.label: Interaction strength
interaction.unit: per population index per synthetic time unit (independent); dimensionless (Eq. 10)
interaction.effect: Sets |A₁₂| in the independent model or a₁₂ in the Eq. 10 example.

initial.label: Initial producer population
initial.effect: Changes the initial value of the first state.

dt.label: Integration step
dt.effect: Both models output every 0.2 synthetic time units.

horizon.label: Simulation horizon
horizon.effect: Sets the final time without changing the step.

noise.label: Multiplicative noise amplitude
noise.unit: per square root of synthetic time
noise.effect: At zero, the independent model follows the deterministic Euler update.

seed.label: Random seed
seed.effect: Initializes the random stream for a repeatable path.

exposure.label: Exposure before withdrawal
exposure.effect: Scales the exposure-dependent loss until the switch.

withdrawal.label: Withdrawal time
withdrawal.effect: Exposure becomes zero at this time. Choose a time within the simulation horizon.

independent.name: Three-population dynamics
independent.equation: dXᵢ = Xᵢ(rᵢ + Σⱼ Aᵢⱼ Xⱼ)dt + σ Xᵢ dWᵢ
independent.citationRole: Eq. 7, p. 11 provides mathematical context only
independent.rationale: Retains PR #9 teaching defaults and [0, 80] projection. The signs provide competition, pest pressure and a beneficial population response.
independent.limits: Coefficients and time are synthetic. No age, delay, impulses or spatial mechanisms. Projection changes the numerical process when crossed.
independent.solver: Explicit Euler–Maruyama with independent normal increments; explicit Euler when σ = 0

coefficientUnits.matrix: per population index per synthetic time unit

withdrawal.name: Exposure withdrawal (Eq. 10 form)
withdrawal.equation: dSᵢ/dt = rᵢSᵢ(1 − Σⱼ aᵢⱼSⱼ/Kᵢ) + mᵢ(Sᵢᵉᑫ − Sᵢ) − εᵢSᵢC(t)
withdrawal.rationale: Author-chosen positive rates, capacities and reference states give two interacting populations. Withdrawal is an illustrative step from the chosen exposure to zero.
withdrawal.limits: No recovered case parameters, measured dose or species-specific calibration. The loss coefficient follows its algebraic role in Eq. 10. The paper's scenario concerns broad pesticide withdrawal.
withdrawal.solver: Explicit Euler, deterministic; seed not used

coefficientUnits.loss: per synthetic exposure index per synthetic time unit
